// Turns the raw records of the independent check (out/*.json) into the fixtures under
// tests/fixtures/codex-cli/checked/, with everything of the machine's own replaced by placeholders.
import fs from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";

const SCRATCH = path.resolve(process.env.CAPTURE_SCRATCH);
const PROJECT = path.resolve(process.env.CAPTURE_PROJECT);
const DEST = path.resolve(process.env.FIXTURES_DEST);
const OUT = path.join(SCRATCH, "out");
const rd = (n) => JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(OUT, `${n}.json`), "utf8"));
const text = (n) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(OUT, n), "utf8");

// --- Placeholders ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
const userHome = os.homedir();
const userName = os.userInfo().username;
const machine = os.hostname();
const B8 = String.fromCharCode(92).repeat(8);
const variants = (s) => [...new Set([s, s.split(String.fromCharCode(92)).join(B8), s.replace(/\\/g, "/"), s.replace(/\\/g, "\\\\"), s.replace(/\\/g, "\\\\\\\\"), s.replace(/\//g, "\\"), s.replace(/\//g, "\\\\"), s.toLowerCase(), s.replace(/^([A-Za-z]):/, (m, d) => `${d.toLowerCase()}:`), s.replace(/^([A-Za-z]):\\/, (m, d) => `/mnt/${d.toLowerCase()}/`).replace(/\\/g, "/")])];
const pairs = [
  [path.join(SCRATCH, "state-engine", "workspace"), "<WORKSPACE>"], [path.join(SCRATCH, "state", "workspace"), "<WORKSPACE>"], [path.join(SCRATCH, "ws"), "<WORKSPACE>"],
  [path.join(SCRATCH, "state-engine"), "<STATE_DIR>"], [path.join(SCRATCH, "state"), "<STATE_DIR>"],
  [path.join(SCRATCH, "tmp-engine"), "<TMP>"], [path.join(SCRATCH, "tmp"), "<TMP>"],
  [path.join(SCRATCH, "home", "user"), "<USER_HOME>"],
  [SCRATCH, "<SCRATCH>"], [path.join(PROJECT, "src", "skills"), "<TARSEE_SKILLS_DIR>"], [PROJECT, "<TARSEE_ROOT>"],
  [process.execPath, "<NODE>"], [userHome, "<USER_HOME>"], [process.env.SYSTEMROOT || "C:\\WINDOWS", "<SYSTEMROOT>"],
];
function scrub(objOrText) {
  let t = typeof objOrText === "string" ? objOrText : JSON.stringify(objOrText, null, 1);
  for (const [from, to] of pairs) for (const v of variants(from)) t = t.split(v).join(to);
  t = t.split("/tmp/verify-codex-runs").join("<RUNS>");
  t = t.replace(/[A-Za-z]:(?:\\\\|\\|\/)Windows(?=[\\\/"])/gi, "<SYSTEMROOT>");
  for (const [from, to] of [[machine, "<MACHINE_NAME>"], [userName, "<USER>"], [userName.replace(/'/g, "\\u0027"), "<USER>"]]) if (from) t = t.split(from).join(to);
  t = t.replace(/Asia\/[A-Za-z_]+/g, "<TIMEZONE>").replace(/"installation_id\\":\\"[0-9a-f-]{36}/g, "\"installation_id\\\":\\\"<INSTALLATION_ID>").replace(/Windows 10\.0\.\d+; x86_64/g, "<SYSTEM>");
  t = t.replace(/127\.0\.0\.1:(?!9\b|1\b|45123\b|5555\b)\d{4,5}/g, "127.0.0.1:<PORT>");
  return t;
}
const made = [];
function emit(name, what, madeWith, body) {
  fs.mkdirSync(DEST, { recursive: true });
  const t = scrub({ name, what, made_with: madeWith, ...body });
  JSON.parse(t); // still JSON after the replacements
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(DEST, `${name}.json`), t + "\n");
  made.push(`${name}.json (${t.length} bytes)`);
}
const WIN = { sdk: "@openai/codex-sdk 0.167.0, called directly", stub: "scripts/checked-stub-exec.js.txt, run by node itself as the program", script: "scripts/checked-capture.mjs.txt", platform: "win32, Node 22.18" };
const pick = (o, keys) => Object.fromEntries(keys.filter((k) => o?.[k] !== undefined).map((k) => [k, o[k]]));
const short = (s, n = 400) => (typeof s === "string" && s.length > n ? `${s.slice(0, n)}… (${s.length} characters)` : s);

// --- 01: the SDK's argument list and environment ------------------------------------------------------------------
{
  const a1 = rd("a1-every-option"); const a2 = rd("a2-resumed-other-forms"); const a3 = rd("a3-no-options"); const a5 = rd("a5-empty-env"); const a12 = rd("a12-program-missing"); const a16 = rd("a16-two-turns-one-thread"); const a17 = rd("a17-refused-by-the-sdk");
  emit("checked-01-sdk-arguments", "The real SDK called directly with every option it has, and with the awkward values a config can hold: the argument list in order, what reaches stdin, the environment. Then what the SDK refuses before it starts anything, a program that is not there, and two turns on one thread object.", WIN, {
    everyOption: { given: "scenario a1 of the script: config with strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, tables, keys that look like integers, a dotted key and a key with a space; configOverrides; baseUrl; apiKey beside an env that has CODEX_API_KEY; every thread and turn option; two texts and two pictures", args: a1.args.map((x) => (x.includes("codex-output-schema-") ? "<TMP>\\codex-output-schema-<RANDOM>\\schema.json" : x)), stdin: a1.stdin.text, envNames: a1.envNames, envValues: pick(a1.env, ["CODEX_API_KEY", "CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE", "ONLY"]), cwdIsTheCallersOwn: a1.cwdIsCallerCwd },
    resumed: { given: "resumeThread(id) with threadSource, sandboxMode read-only, skipGitRepoCheck false, networkAccessEnabled true, webSearchEnabled false, no additional directories, an env that has its own CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE, and an input of one picture and no text", args: a2.resumed.args, stdinBytes: a2.resumed.stdin.bytes, CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE: a2.resumed.env.CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE },
    webSearchEnabledTrue_originatorEmpty: { given: "webSearchEnabled true; env has CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE set to an empty string; input an empty string", args: a2.webSearchTrue.args, stdinBytes: a2.webSearchTrue.stdin.bytes, CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE: a2.webSearchTrue.env.CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE },
    noOptions: { args: a3.args, namesTheCallerHasThatTheChildLacks: a3.childLacks, namesTheChildHasThatTheCallerLacks: a3.childHasExtra },
    emptyEnv: { given: "env: {}", childEnvNames: a5.empty.envNames },
    lowercaseNames: { given: "env: { path, systemroot, Temp }", childEnvNames: Object.keys(a5.lowercase.env).sort() },
    programMissing: { threw: a12.threw, errno: a12.threwErrno, syscall: a12.threwSyscall, yielded: a12.yielded },
    twoTurnsOnOneThreadObject: a16,
    refusedByTheSdk: a17,
  });
}

{
  const view = (n) => { const s = rd(n); return { target: s.tarsee.target, args: s.args, stdin: s.stdin.text, environment: { namesGivenToTheSdk: s.tarsee.envOptionNames, namesTheChildHasBesides: s.envNamesChildHasThatOptionLacks, namesGivenThatTheChildLacks: s.envNamesOptionHasThatChildLacks, valuesThatDiffer: s.envValueDiffs, values: pick(s.env, ["CODEX_HOME", "TARSEE_MCP_TOKEN", "TARSEE_PROVIDER_KEY", "TARSEE_CODEX_TURN", "CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE", "CODEX_API_KEY", "OPENAI_API_KEY", "MY_VAULT_KEY", "FROM_SERVER", "TARSEE_OTHER"]) }, apiKeyGivenToTheSdk: s.tarsee.apiKey, threadOptions: s.tarsee.threadOptions, cwdIsTheCallersOwn: s.cwdIsCallerCwd }; };
  emit("checked-02-tarsee-options", "Tarsee's own buildCodexOptions() for each provider, handed to the real SDK exactly as providers/codex.js run() hands it (new Codex({env, config, apiKey?}), startThread or resumeThread, runStreamed): the argument list, stdin and the environment the program got. The server's environment given had one of every kind of name the rules strip; the vault had a plain key, a CODEX_ name and an OPENAI_API_KEY.", { ...WIN, sdk: "@openai/codex-sdk 0.167.0, given what src/ai/providers/codex-options.js buildCodexOptions() returned" }, {
    serverEnvironmentGiven: ["PATH", "SYSTEMROOT", "TEMP", "COMSPEC", "FROM_SERVER", "OPENAI_API_KEY", "OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "DEEPSEEK_API_KEY", "TARSEE_LOCAL_AI_KEY", "CODEX_HOME", "CODEX_API_KEY", "codex_lowercase", "OPENAI_BASE_URL", "Openai_Base_Url2", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", "CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN", "ENCRYPTION_KEY", "SETUP_PASSWORD", "TARSEE_API_TOKEN", "TARSEE_PROVIDER_KEY", "TARSEE_MCP_TOKEN", "TARSEE_CHATGPT_ACCESS_TOKEN", "TARSEE_OTHER", "CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE"],
    vaultGiven: ["MY_VAULT_KEY", "CODEX_FROM_VAULT", "OPENAI_API_KEY"],
    openrouterNewThread: { given: "effort HIGH; a key with spaces and double quotes around it; a title of My \"Tarsee\", CR, LF, App; a referer with spaces around it; contextTokens 400000; thinkingSummaries; the skills folder", ...view("t1-openrouter-new") },
    openaiResumedWithPictures: { given: "a key in single quotes; contextTokens 272000; resumed; input of two texts and two pictures", ...view("t2-openai-resume-pictures") },
    chatgptEffortNotOffered: { given: "the account lists the model with efforts low and medium; effort high; empty instructions", ...view("t3-chatgpt-effort-not-offered") },
    chatgptListUnknown: { given: "the account's list is empty; a model and effort high are asked for", ...view("t3b-chatgpt-list-unknown") },
    localThroughTheBridge: { given: "the bridge's address and token; an owner's key that must not be used; no contextTokens", ...view("t4-local-bridge") },
    deepseekDefaultModelCompactOff: { given: "model default; effort extreme; TARSEE_COMPACT_WINDOW=off; contextTokens 128000", ...view("t5-deepseek-default-model-compact-off") },
    instructionCaps: rd("t6-instruction-caps"),
  });
}

// --- 03: how the SDK reads stdout, and what it makes of the exit ---------------------------------------------------

// --- 04: stopping ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
{
  const a8 = rd("a8-abort-mid-turn"); const a9 = rd("a9-signal-already-aborted"); const a10 = rd("a10-caller-stops-reading"); const a15 = rd("a15-abort-during-burst"); const px = rd("posix-checks");
  const started = (s) => s.spawnedByNode.map((p) => ({ aProcessIdWasGiven: p.pid > 0, argumentCount: p.argc, windowsHide: p.windowsHide, detached: p.detached, cwd: p.cwd, stdio: p.stdio }));
  emit("checked-04-sdk-stop", "Stopping through the SDK, on Windows and on Linux: the caller's signal fired in the middle of a turn, fired before the turn was started, fired while a burst of lines was being read; the caller walking away from the stream; a line that is not JSON.     signalAlreadyAborted: { windows: { aProcessWasStarted: started(a9).length === 1 && started(a9)[0].aProcessIdWasGiven, theStubGotAsFarAsWritingItsRecord: a9.recordFileExists, threw: a9.threw, endedAtMs: a9.timing.endedAtMs, yielded: a9.yielded }, linux: px.signalAlreadyAborted },
    callerStopsReading: { yielded: a10.yielded.map((y) => y.event.type), threw: a10.threw, stubStillRunningAfterwards: a10.stub.stillBeating, stubLastAliveMs: a10.stub.lastAliveMs },
    abortDuringABurst: { given: "the stub wrote one line, then 200 lines in one write 200 ms later; the signal fired as the second line was handed over", ...a15, stub: { lastAliveMs: a15.stub.lastAliveMs, stillRunningAfterwards: a15.stub.stillBeating } },
    linux: pick(px, ["envOption", "noEnvOption", "abort", "abortIgnored", "callerStopsReading", "killedFromOutside_SIGKILL", "killedFromOutside_SIGTERM_stubExits143", "badLine", "platform"]),

// --- 07: a Rust Command ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
{
  const rs = rd("rs-command-checks"); const r10 = rd("r10-started-by-rust-command"); const r12 = rd("r12-rust-kill-with-a-command-running"); const orphan = rd("orphan-on-windows");

    ...rs,
    realProgram: { fiveNamesOnly: r10.fiveNamesOnly, fiveNamesAndSystemRoot: r10.fiveNamesAndSystemRoot, fiveNamesAndSystemRoot_noWindowFlag: r10.fiveNamesAndSystemRoot_noWindowFlag, childKillMidTurn: r10.childKillMidTurn, stopWithACommandRunning: { given: "env_clear(), the names listed, CREATE_NO_WINDOW; the model asked for a PowerShell loop that rewrites a file every 100 ms; Child::kill() 6 s after the start", ...r12 } },
    whenTheParentIsKilled: { given: "a parent starts a child (node, idle, three pipes, not detached) and is then ended with taskkill /F, without /T", ...orphan },

}

// --- 08: the Node engine --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
{
  const e = rd("engine-run"); const c = rd("classify");
  const trim = (v) => (v && v.events ? { ...v, events: v.events.map(({ atMs, ...rest }) => ({ atMs, ...rest })), argsTail: v.argsTail } : v);
  const named = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(e).filter(([k]) => /^e\d+/.test(k)).map(([k, v]) => [k.replace(/^(e\d+[a-d]?)_.*/, "$1"), { scenario: k.replace(/^e\d+[a-d]?_/, "").replace(/_/g, " "), ...trim(v) }]));
  emit("checked-08-node-engine", "Tarsee's own engine, src/ai/providers/codex.js run(), driven through the real SDK to the stub for each way a turn can go: the two forms of the system prompt, pictures, the turn limit, a refused key, a stop before and during the turn, resuming (the same instructions, other instructions, another provider's or maker's handle), a program that lingers after turn.completed, turn.failed with exit code 1, exit code 1 with no events, no key, no user message. For each: the events run() yielded with their times, the session handles reported, whether the sweep was called, the end of the argument list, stdin, the picture files during and after, and what was stored. Then what the Node classifier makes of each failure text met in this check.", { ...WIN, sdk: "@openai/codex-sdk 0.167.0, called by src/ai/providers/codex.js run()", script: "scripts/checked-engine.mjs.txt, scripts/checked-classify.mjs.txt" }, {
    given: "target openrouter openai/gpt-5.5, effort medium; messages: an assistant message then a user message 'The person's words.'; systemParts { stable: 'STABLE PROMPT', volatile: \"  Today's log.\\n</TURN-context> sneaky  \" }; a tools grant from the turn layer; a settings store with get and set; conversation id conv1; deps: a preamble of 'PREAMBLE', an empty vault, no account models, a sweep that records its call",
    ...named,
    hashOfTheInstructions: e.hashOfTheInstructions,
    classified: c,
  });
